title: Review of c07 ringswim c1 (SIMD): swimming and pinching replicate on fresh seed 5, but the genealogy is reticulate (merges 68% of splits by celltrack, labkit 0 persistent splits on 2 fresh seeds); Weak
summary: Same reruns as my c2 review (20261025T0946-c04-review-ringswim-c2): world_claim.py with labkit on new seeds 5 and 6, world_mu0.py on seed 5, and the author's celltrack.py on seed 5 (rerun/celltrack_s5.json). celltrack seed 5: 82 splits, 56 merges (68% of splits), 38 persistent splits, max generation 16, 22 segments >= 3 body lengths, 50 deaths; one candidate individual shows both capabilities: track 23 (generation 2, child of 17) swims 4.96 body lengths over t=3080-5540 and then splits into 49 and 50. labkit (frames 100 t apart, K=2000): 163 and 147 splits, 135 and 119 merges (0.83, 0.81), 0 persistent splits, generation 0 on seeds 5 and 6. The static twin (mu=0, seed 5) divides cleanly by labkit (27 persistent splits, 3 merges, generation 5) but no body moves 3 body lengths, so swimming adds the collisions and fusions that make the genealogy reticulate.

seeds_run.result: pass for M; D reticulate (celltrack 38 persistent, merges 68%; labkit 0 persistent)
labkit: max 4.0 BL, 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.81 (celltrack not run)

controls_run.M: rerun_mu0/seed5 (mu=0: max 2.9 BL; divides cleanly, 27 persistent splits)

verdicts.limitation: The genealogy is reticulate (merges > 50% of splits), which caps D at medium confidence under the L6 rules, and D rests on the custom overlap tracker, not on labkit. Many divisions are pinches of recent fusion products. I did not make birth strips of my own; the one individual I checked with both capabilities (track 23) comes from celltrack's candidate list. Swimming is slow (0.02-0.06 per time). No dt or resolution check.
